questions.question_text: Form the partial differential equation by eliminating arbitrary constant $a$ and $b$ from $z=(x^2+a)(y^2+b)$.
questions.answer: Differentiation gives $p=2x(y^2+b)$ and $q=2y(x^2+a)$; hence $pq=4xyz$.

questions.question_text: If $f(x)=x^2$ in $-\pi\le x\le\pi$, then find the RMS value of the function $f(x)$.
questions.answer: $\sqrt{(1/2\pi)\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}x^4\,dx}=\pi^2/\sqrt5$.

questions.question_text: Write all possible solutions of one dimensional heat equation.
questions.answer: Separation of $u_t=\alpha^2u_{xx}$ gives trigonometric modes $(A\cos kx+B\sin kx)e^{-\alpha^2k^2t}$, linear steady modes $Ax+B$, and hyperbolic modes $(Ae^{kx}+Be^{-kx})e^{\alpha^2k^2t}$. Boundary and initial data select their superposition.

questions.question_text: Define self reciprocal function with example.
questions.answer: A function is self reciprocal under a transform if its transform has the same functional form. For the normalized Fourier cosine or sine transform, $x^{-1/2}$ transforms to $s^{-1/2}$ for $s>0$.

questions.question_text: Find the Z-transform of $a^n\cos n\pi$.
questions.answer: $a^n\cos n\pi=(-a)^n$, so $Z=z/(z+a)$ for $|z|>|a|$.

Solve $\sqrt p+\sqrt q=1$.
questions.answer: Set $\sqrt p=a$, $\sqrt q=1-a$, with $0\le a\le1$. A complete integral is $z=a^2x+(1-a)^2y+b$.

questions.question_text: (i) Obtain the partial differential equation by eliminating arbitrary function $f$ from $z=xy+f(x^2+y^2+z^2)$. (ii) Solve $(D^2-2DD\prime+D\prime^2)z=\cos(x-3y)$.
questions.answer: (i) Differentiation gives $(p-y)/(x+zp)=(q-x)/(y+zq)$, hence $(p-y)(y+zq)=(q-x)(x+zp)$. (ii) The operator is $(D-D\prime)^2$, so $z=\phi(x+y)+x\psi(x+y)-\cos(x-3y)/16$.

questions.question_text: Solve (i) $(y-z)p+(z-x)q=x-y$ (ii) $p^2+q^2=x^2+y^2$.
questions.answer: (i) The characteristics preserve $x+y+z$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2$, hence $\Phi(x+y+z,x^2+y^2+z^2)=0$. (ii) Separate $p^2-x^2=a$ and $q^2-y^2=-a$: a complete integral is $z=\int^x\sqrt{t^2+a}\,dt+\int^y\sqrt{t^2-a}\,dt+b$, with independent sign branches and real domains.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier series upto third harmonic from the following data: $x=0,\pi/3,2\pi/3,\pi,4\pi/3,5\pi/3,2\pi$; $y=1,1.4,1.9,1.7,1.5,1.2,1$.
questions.answer: Using the six distinct equally spaced values and discrete Fourier coefficients gives $a_0/2=29/20$, $a_1=-11/30$, $b_1=\sqrt3/10$, $a_2=-1/10$, $b_2=-\sqrt3/30$, and Nyquist cosine coefficient $1/60$. Thus $y\approx29/20-(11/30)\cos x+(\sqrt3/10)\sin x-(1/10)\cos2x-(\sqrt3/30)\sin2x+(1/60)\cos3x$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier series of periodicity $2\pi$ for $f(x)=x$ for $0<x<\pi$, $f(x)=2\pi-x$ for $\pi<x<2\pi$, and hence deduce $1+1/3^2+1/5^2+\cdots=\pi^2/8$.
questions.answer: The periodic function is $|x|$ on $(-\pi,\pi)$, so $f(x)=\pi/2-(4/\pi)\sum_{k\ge0}\cos((2k+1)x)/(2k+1)^2$. At $x=0$, the sum is $\pi^2/8$.

questions.question_text: A tightly stretched string with fixed end points $x=0$ and $x=l$ is initially at rest in its equilibrium position. If it is set vibrating giving each point a velocity $3x(l-x)$, find the displacement.
questions.answer: The initial-velocity sine coefficients are $12l^2[1-(-1)^n]/(n^3\pi^3)$. With wave speed $c$, $y=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{12l^3[1-(-1)^n]}{c n^4\pi^4}\sin(n\pi x/l)\sin(n\pi ct/l)$.

questions.question_text: A rod of length $l$ has its ends A and B kept at 0°C and 100°C until steady state condition prevail. If the temperature at B is reduced suddenly to 0°C and kept so while that of A is maintained, find the temperature $u(x,t)$ at a distance $x$ from A at time $t$.
questions.answer: The initial profile is $100x/l$ and both ends subsequently vanish. Its sine coefficients are $200(-1)^{n+1}/(n\pi)$. Thus $u(x,t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{200(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi}\sin(n\pi x/l)e^{-\alpha^2n^2\pi^2t/l^2}$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier cosine transform of $e^{-ax}$, $a>0$ and hence evaluate $\int_0^\infty dx/(a^2+x^2)^2$.
questions.answer: $F_c(e^{-ax})=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,a/(a^2+s^2)$. Parseval yields $\int_0^\infty e^{-2ax}dx=(2a^2/\pi)\int_0^\infty ds/(a^2+s^2)^2$, hence the integral is $\pi/(4a^3)$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier transform of $f(x)=1$ for $|x|<a$ and $0$ for $|x|>a>0$, and hence evaluate $\int_0^\infty(\sin x)/x\,dx$.
questions.answer: For the unnormalized convention $F(s)=2\sin(as)/s$. Inversion at the origin gives $1=(2/\pi)\int_0^\infty\sin(as)/s\,ds$, hence the integral equals $\pi/2$.
The roots are $1,2$, so $x_n=A+B2^n$. The initial conditions give $A=-1,B=1$, hence $x_n=2^n-1$.

questions.question_text: (i) Find $Z\{(n+1)(n+2)/2\}$. (ii) Find the inverse Z-transform of $z/[(z-1)(z-2)]$ using residues.
questions.answer: (i) The binomial generating series gives $Z=(1-z^{-1})^{-3}=z^3/(z-1)^3$. (ii) The residues, equivalently the partial fractions $z/(z-2)-z/(z-1)$, give $x_n=2^n-1$ for $n\ge0$.
